metadata.rules_text:
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce forecasted values by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days post-spike.
- Underestimates mean-reversion zones; if recent 18-day average is > 75, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 7–10 days.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices; apply downward correction of 3–6% for the first 10 days of forecast.
- Overshoots after volatility spikes (e.g., 80+ → 85+); cap forecast at +5% above recent 7-day high for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >85 for 3+ consecutive days), model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–4% for next 5–7 days if sentiment remains neutral or positive.
- Horizon-specific: Day 1–3 forecasts are consistently too high; apply 3–7% downward adjustment for first 3 days regardless of sentiment.
- If sentiment history is non-zero (even small), model should adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction; if sentiment > 0.2, increase forecast by 1–3%; if < -0.2, decrease by 1–3%.
